title: Rip a short pine board past a running table saw with a push stick
instruction: Cut the pine board lengthwise along the fence so that a 40 mm strip comes off, then leave both pieces lying flat on the table.
context: Ripping stock on a table saw is routine carpenter work (O*NET 47-2031.00, about 700,000 US workers, BLS OEWS May 2023). The board is fed with a push stick so the hand stays clear of the blade. Two hands are needed: one holds the board down and to the fence against the cutting loads, the other feeds it. Unlike #586 (relief block at a saw fence) and #1245 (paper guillotine, hand clear), one arm feeds with a tool while the other holds down.
setup: Positions in cm in the station frame (x forward, y left, table top 74.75 cm). Cast-iron saw table 60 x 107 x 3 cm (x 12..72, y -62..45) with an aluminium rip fence face at x 18.5 (3 x 107 x 4.5 cm); total 142.6 kg, one rigid body. Saw blade: 10 in, 2.4 mm plate, 25 mm above the table, 15 cm long at the table, red teeth, x 22.66, y 10.5..25.5. Red stop line y 0.5. Pine board 1.9 x 8.9 x 22 cm in two pieces with a 3.2 mm kerf: strip 4.0 cm wide (83.6 g) at x 18.5..22.5 and offcut 4.58 cm wide (95.7 g) at x 22.82..27.4, both y -12..10, friction 0.30, against the fence. Push stick: pine, 115 g, forked heel (two 2 cm deep blocks with a 14 mm gap), 40 cm bar riding 3 mm above the blade top, 5 x 1.2 x 5 cm upright grip fin 33 cm behind the heel, lying on the saw table at x 36, heel front face y -20.
scoring: Measured at the end, perfect state held 1 s. 0 if a gripper fingertip, gripper link or TCP is ever within 100 mm in plan of the blade while below 150 mm above the saw table, the push stick touches the blade plate, a piece leaves the table, or a piece is kicked more than 30 mm up. 0.25 if the board front is 30 mm into the blade (or the board was lifted more than 4 mm over the blade). 0.5 if the cut is complete (both rear ends 12 mm past the blade's back edge) but a piece is not flat or the strip width at the blade is more than 6.4 mm off 40 mm. 0.75 if complete, flat, width within 6.4 mm but a gripper is within 30 mm of a piece, a piece is moving, or width is not within 3.2 mm. 1.0 if complete, strip 40 +- 3.2 mm, both pieces flat (tilt <= 8 degrees) and still, both grippers at least 30 mm from the pieces and 100 mm from the blade.
reset_notes: Strip and offcut against the fence, front ends 5 mm before the blade; push stick lying on the saw table to the right of the board; blade and fence fixed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, PhysX 240 Hz. Real-size saw table, fence, 10 in blade, 3.2 mm kerf, 19x89x220 mm pine, 400 mm push stick. Blade and cut are code: the blade is a non-colliding marker, the board is two pieces with the real kerf. Side, lift and yaw loads on the strip are coded, well below real feed forces (arms stall near 7 N), set so an unheld board leaves the fence. No rotation, sawdust, guard or riving knife.
